title: Review steps that finished after the permit was issued
question: Were any permits issued while a review station that had already received the plans had not yet signed off?
finding: Of 10,015 permits issued 2020 to 2026 that appear in both tables, 13 have a review step that arrived before the issue date but finished a day or more after it (13 steps), and 2 were issued with a step that arrived before issue and still has no finish date.
how: The issuance table gives each permit’s issue date; the review table gives each station visit. A step is counted when it arrived on or before the issue date and finished one or more days after it, or has no finish date at all. Rows are joined on the permit number and the addendum number.
limits: A late finish date is often clerical: the reviewer approved at the counter and closed the record later, or the step belongs to a revision filed under the same number. The Building Code has site permits issued before their addenda (section 106A.3.4.2.3, quoted in the code-rules analysis). The table does not say whether a later step changed anything.

sources.t: DataSF: Building Permit Application Review Metrics (Building Inspection; table as of 17 Nov 2026)
DataSF: Building Permit Application Issuance Metrics (Building Inspection; table as of 17 Nov 2026)
